_metadata.independence: I read only u04-correction-input.json; no other file, repository search, web lookup or API was used.

hints.reason: An apple-tree branch on one side and a bank branch on the other, both everyday senses.

best_available.why: Clean double meaning that lands on both targets without explanation.

pairs.pair_note: Single hint, and it is a good one; nothing further needed.

hints.reason: Apple tree is immediate; bears climbing or scratching trees is a familiar image but TREE alone points at many animals before BEAR.
A shared scene (bear raiding a picnic basket, Yogi Bear style) with apples as classic basket food, but neither side is the first thing PICNIC evokes.
Honey is the bear's food (Pooh); apples dipped in honey (Rosh Hashanah) or honey-baked apples is a real but secondary pairing for APPLE.

best_available.why: The APPLE side is certain and a bear in a tree is a widely known image; it is the least lopsided of three borderline hints.

pairs.pair_note: No hint reaches PASS; all three are plausible shared scenes with one weak side. TREE or PICNIC would be serviceable.

hints.reason: An apple for the teacher is a stock image; the school bell (or the teacher's hand bell) completes the same classroom scene.

best_available.why: One classroom scene covers both targets; the bell side is slightly less direct than the apple side.

pairs.pair_note: Passes on the shared-scene route; BELL via school is a step but a familiar one.

hints.reason: Brooklyn Bridge is direct; APPLE is reached through Big Apple (New York), a two-step geography route the owner has accepted as fair.

best_available.why: Only hint, and a fair geography route per the anchor.

pairs.pair_note: Fair rather than strong; the apple side depends on the Big Apple nickname.

hints.reason: Apple gift cards are a ubiquitous product (Apple the company), and gift card is a compound for CARD.
Credit card is direct; Apple Card is a credit card, which many but not all players will know.

best_available.why: Apple gift cards are more universally known than Apple Card.

pairs.pair_note: Both use Apple the company, consistent with the owner's SOFTWARE/SIRI precedent.

hints.reason: Both sides go through Snow White (the poisoned apple, the queen's castle); the castle is the story's setting but not its iconic element, and SNOW alone reads as weather.
Snow White again for APPLE (plus white apple flesh), and White Castle the burger brand or pale stone walls for CASTLE; each link is a step away.

best_available.why: SNOW evokes Snow White more readily than WHITE does, and that story is the only real bridge between apple and castle.

pairs.pair_note: Both hints are the same Snow White route split in half; neither lands cleanly. A hint that names the story more directly would serve better.

hints.reason: Gala is a well-known apple variety, but a gala is just a formal event; the leap to CROWN (royalty attend galas) is invented to rescue the word.

best_available.why: The only hint; serviceable for APPLE but it does not point at CROWN.

pairs.pair_note: Reject. Needs a new hint (e.g. something from a shared royal or fairy-tale scene) rather than GALA.

hints.reason: Diamonds are the archetype of shiny; a polished shiny apple is a familiar image but apple is far from the first shiny thing a player names.
Cutting an apple into slices is everyday; diamond cut is a standard jewellery term.
Baseball diamond is direct; APPLE arrives only via the phrase 'apple pie and baseball' or old slang for the ball, which not every player will make.
Big Apple is a strong compound; 'big diamond' is just an adjective on a ring, nothing specific to DIAMOND.

best_available.why: Both senses are direct and common; no explanation needed.

pairs.pair_note: CUT carries the pair; the other three are each half-strong.

hints.reason: Hot dog is a compound; hot apple pie and hot apple cider are familiar phrases that make APPLE reachable, if second.

best_available.why: Hot dog is instant and hot apple cider/pie gives a fair route to APPLE.

pairs.pair_note: Passes on the familiar-phrase rule; the apple side is a genuine but weaker phrase.

hints.reason: Apple pie is the archetypal pie; fish pie is a real, well-known dish in Britain though less so elsewhere.

best_available.why: Compound on both sides; fish pie is the only recognizability risk.

pairs.pair_note: Passes; strength depends on the player's familiarity with fish pie.

hints.reason: Cider is made from apples; it is served in a glass, which is a scene rather than a compound but a recognizable one.
Apple juice is a compound and a glass of juice (juice glass) is an everyday scene.

best_available.why: Apple juice is more universal than cider and the glass is implicit in the drink.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass per the anchors; JUICE is the stronger serve.

hints.reason: Red/Golden Delicious are the best-known apple variety names; GOLD is reached through Golden Delicious by ordinary inflection.

best_available.why: Valid per the anchor; the gold side relies on the Golden Delicious variety.

pairs.pair_note: Valid, moderate recognizability.

hints.reason: A red apple and a red heart are both iconic colour images, not incidental descriptions, so the colour route is fair here despite being a colour.

best_available.why: Both targets are red in their emblematic form.

pairs.pair_note: A colour hint that works because both words are colour-defined icons; still broad enough that players may hit other red things first.

hints.reason: Honey is the definition of sweet; apples are sweet but also tart, so SWEET names honey first and apple only loosely.
Honey bee is direct; bees pollinating apple blossom is true and known but not what a player reaches for from BEE.

best_available.why: Both sides are reachable without specialist knowledge, which BEE's apple side needs.

pairs.pair_note: Neither hint is strong; apple-and-honey as a dipped pairing is the real shared scene but no hint names it.

hints.reason: Feeding a horse an apple as a treat is a single recognizable scene that supplies both words at once.

best_available.why: Shared feeding scene per the anchor.

pairs.pair_note: Passes on the scene route; each word alone is only loosely 'treat'.

hints.reason: Frost is a near-synonym of ice; the apple link (frost damaging orchards or blossom) is a grower's fact an ordinary player will not make.

best_available.why: Only hint; it will reach ICE but not APPLE.

pairs.pair_note: Reject; a hint around a shared scene (e.g. a cold drink or dessert) would serve better.

hints.reason: The Command (⌘) key is widely known as the Mac-specific modifier (Cmd+C), so it reaches APPLE through Apple the company and KEY directly.

best_available.why: The Command key is familiar enough as an Apple key to be fair, though non-Mac users may need a beat.

pairs.pair_note: Passes under the Apple-the-company precedent; recognizability is moderate, not broad.

hints.reason: A king is royal by definition; APPLE is reached only via the Royal Gala variety, well known in some markets and barely in others.

best_available.why: Only hint; fine for KING, thin for APPLE.

pairs.pair_note: Borderline because the apple side depends on a regional variety name.

hints.reason: Knight in shining armour is a set phrase; a polished shining apple is a real image but far from the first thing SHINING evokes.

best_available.why: Only hint; strong for KNIGHT, weak for APPLE.

pairs.pair_note: Lopsided; the apple side is a generic surface descriptor.

hints.reason: Newton's apple is famous; Newton's prism work on light is schoolbook fact but it is a second, separate fact about the man rather than one shared story.

best_available.why: Only hint; a knowledgeable player gets both, a casual one gets only APPLE.

pairs.pair_note: Borderline: a named person linking two unrelated facts is weaker than the single gravity story that makes NEWTON work for APPLE+MOON.

hints.reason: The falling apple and the orbiting moon are the two halves of Newton's own gravity story, so one familiar tale supplies both targets.

best_available.why: A single shared story (gravity: apple falls, moon orbits) rather than two facts.

pairs.pair_note: Passes on the shared-story route; the moon half is slightly less automatic than the apple half.

hints.reason: Queen bee is a compound; apple needs the pollination fact, which is true but not a player's first thought.
Snow White is one story whose two most famous elements are the evil queen and the poisoned apple; SNOW alone first reads as weather, costing a little fairness.
Poison apple is a set phrase and the queen is the poisoner in the same Snow White story, matching the owner's EVE anchor.
Evil Queen is a compound; the apple is reached only after thinking of that queen, so the apple side is one step removed.

best_available.why: Set phrase for APPLE and the queen's deed in the same story; broadest recognizability.

pairs.pair_note: POISON and SNOW both work through Snow White; EVIL is a weaker cut of the same route and BEE is lopsided.

hints.reason: Hard rock is a compound; APPLE is reachable only through 'hard cider' (a second step) or a crisp apple, neither of which a player will make from HARD.
Apple core is a compound; ROCK via rock core samples or the Earth's rocky interior is real but a geology step most players will not take.

best_available.why: Certain for APPLE and defensible for ROCK; HARD does not reach APPLE at all.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; CORE is usable if the pair must ship, HARD should be dropped.

hints.reason: Apple tree is immediate; a tree casting its shade or shadow is a familiar scene, but SHADOW is not what a player first attaches to TREE.

best_available.why: Only hint; the apple side is solid and the shadow side is a recognizable scene even if secondary.

pairs.pair_note: Borderline on the scene route; shade rather than shadow is the natural word, which weakens the b side.
